title: A Year of Agents | Armin Ronacher | CodeCrafts 2026
summary: Armin Ronacher on a year of building with and building agents: real power, but agent psychosis, slop PRs, lost understanding and the need for deliberate friction.

assertions.quote: I said like I would be challenged if it's more than 10%. And that was that was completely invalidated

verdicts.note: Agentic tools clearly expanded what AI can do unaided, and METR's 2026 update suggests speedups are now likely, but measured average gains remain modest.

assertions.quote: why do these open source projects get these random pull requests? Well, it is because it can

verdicts.note: Maintainers of curl, Ghostty and others document floods of low-effort AI PRs and reports, and GitHub added tooling to restrict PRs in response.

assertions.quote: I increasingly have a problem when infrastructure core components are being written with the power of AI and no human that understands that anymore

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: a lot of stuff gets merged without reviews

verdicts.note: Surveys (e.g. Sonar 2026) report many developers don't always check AI code before committing, despite saying they distrust it.

assertions.quote: agents really are all about writing code, running code and doing that

verdicts.note: Tool-using agents that run code beat pure text reasoning on calculation and data tasks, and verifiable coding rewards drove recent agent training gains.

Google: splitting migrations into simpler, well-defined sub-steps (each validated by build/tests) speeds iteration, and LLMs are very good at fixing a well-defined problem; this supports decomposition into verifiable steps in a pipeline setting.

assertions.quote: how much can you throw into an LLM before it falls apart? Um not a lot it turns out

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: they're going to write duplicated code left and right

verdicts.note: GitClear's 2024-25 analyses found rising duplicated code and falling refactoring with AI adoption.

assertions.quote: the agent will do things that it shouldn't be doing, unsurprisingly

verdicts.note: Agents have deleted files and run destructive commands when unrestricted; vendors themselves recommend containers/VMs for skip-permissions modes.

assertions.quote: went wrong in your process if if the agent had the the power to do that

verdicts.note: Agents violate explicit instructions often enough that dev/prod separation, permissions and sandboxes are standard advice; Replit's own fix was architectural.

assertions.quote: There was a leaderboard within meta who spends the most amount of tokens.

verdicts.note: Goodhart's law applies: Orosz reports leaderboards and spend targets at large firms prompting busywork; consistent with past experience of line-of-code metrics.

assertions.quote: if you take the second law of thermodynamics, everything decays towards chaos

verdicts.note: Consistent with long-horizon benchmarks such as SlopCodeBench and with studies of AI-code churn and duplication. Evidence is early but points the same way.
